finalText:
Five small files, one straight-through request flow.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[server.js] -->|checks token| B[auth.js]
  A --> C[routes.js]
  C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
  C -->|writes| E[store.js]
  D --> E
```

- `server.js` opens the HTTP server and rejects anyone without a valid token.
- `auth.js` checks bearer tokens shaped `userId.signature`, signed with `AUTH_SECRET`.
- `routes.js` maps method and path to a handler: users and orders, reads and one write.
- `cache.js` is a small 256-entry LRU sitting in front of reads, no expiry of its own.
- `store.js` is an in-memory stand-in database, each record expires 15 minutes after it's written.

One thing worth knowing: `routes.js` says writes should invalidate cache keys, but `putOrder` never does. So a new order can be invisible until the cached `orders:<id>` entry ages out of the LRU on its own.
